rules.secretRule: Never store credential values in this catalog, Baton project content, MCP resources, docs, or chat. Use each resource credentialAuthority.

resources.label: Repository
resources.purpose: Source-of-truth repository for this project.
resources.obtain: Open the repository in GitHub and copy owner/repository from its URL.
resources.validation: owner/repository, using GitHub-safe repository characters.
resources.security: Bind the repository separately from the account credential so child projects can override only the resource they need.

resources.label: Fine-grained personal access token
resources.purpose: Reusable GitHub identity for repository automation.
resources.obtain: GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Fine-grained tokens. Restrict repositories and permissions to the minimum needed.
resources.validation: A GitHub fine-grained token; Baton seals it before persistence.
resources.security: Prefer hosted OAuth when available. Never put the token in project notes, env examples, logs, or client-visible fields.

resources.label: Vercel project
resources.purpose: Frontend deployment target.
resources.obtain: Open Vercel Dashboard → Project → Settings and use the project name or project ID.
resources.validation: Project name/ID accepted by the Vercel API.
resources.security: Keep the reusable account at workspace level and bind only the project resource here.

resources.label: Team ID
resources.purpose: Disambiguates a Vercel project owned by a team.
resources.obtain: Vercel Dashboard → Team Settings → General and copy the Team ID when the project is team-owned.
resources.validation: Vercel team identifier; leave empty for personal-scope projects.
resources.security: This is an identifier, not a secret.

resources.label: Vercel access token
resources.purpose: Reusable server-side Vercel identity.
resources.obtain: Vercel Account Settings → Tokens. Create a dedicated token for Baton automation.
resources.validation: Vercel access token accepted by the API.
resources.security: Store only through Baton's sealed credential path; never in project content.

resources.label: Convex team ID
resources.purpose: Stable team scope for Convex Management API operations.
resources.obtain: Convex Dashboard → Team Settings. Use the team ID shown with access-token settings.
resources.validation: Convex numeric/string team ID accepted by /v1/teams/:team_id endpoints.
resources.security: Identifier only. Pair with a team token only when automation is required.

resources.label: Convex team access token
resources.purpose: Reusable Management API authority for projects, deployments, and custom-domain orchestration.
resources.obtain: Convex Dashboard → Team Settings → Access Tokens. For long-lived automation, prefer a dedicated service-account team member.
resources.validation: Bearer token that can list projects for the configured team ID.
resources.security: High-value secret. Baton encrypts it server-side; never copy it into project docs, client logs, or frontend environment variables.

resources.label: Convex project
resources.purpose: Backend project identity inside the owning Convex team.
resources.obtain: Convex Dashboard → select the project and copy its project slug/ID.
resources.validation: Project slug/ID belonging to the configured Convex team.
resources.security: Treat project identity as metadata; deployment credentials remain separate.

resources.label: Production deployment
resources.purpose: Specific Convex production deployment used by this project.
resources.obtain: Convex Dashboard → Project → production deployment. The default hostname also contains the deployment name before .convex.cloud.
resources.validation: Lowercase Convex deployment name such as aromatic-warbler-842.
resources.security: This is an identifier; the deploy key is separate and secret.

resources.label: Production deploy key
resources.purpose: Deployment-scoped authority used by CI/Vercel/CLI to push Convex code.
resources.obtain: Convex Dashboard → Project/Deployment Settings → deploy keys, or create one through the authorized Management API.
resources.validation: Convex deploy key matching the selected production deployment.
resources.security: Project-scoped secret. Keep it in Vercel/CI or Baton's sealed project binding; do not inherit it unless the parent explicitly shares that deployment.

resources.label: Convex function/API custom domain
resources.purpose: Custom hostname used for Convex function/API traffic and optionally as the canonical CONVEX_CLOUD_URL.
resources.obtain: Choose an owned subdomain, then Convex Deployment Settings → Custom Domains. Convex returns the DNS records required for verification.
resources.validation: FQDN you control, e.g. api.example.com.
resources.security: Use a dedicated backend subdomain. Only make it canonical after DNS/TLS verification and frontend redeploy planning.

resources.label: Convex HTTP Actions custom domain
resources.purpose: Custom hostname for Convex HTTP Actions and optionally the canonical CONVEX_SITE_URL used by auth callbacks/issuers.
resources.obtain: Choose an owned subdomain, then add it under Convex Deployment Settings → Custom Domains and apply the DNS records Convex returns.
resources.validation: FQDN you control, e.g. auth.example.com or convex.example.com.
resources.security: Changing CONVEX_SITE_URL can affect Convex Auth redirect URLs and token issuer; update auth-provider allowlists before making it canonical.

resources.label: Cloudflare API token
resources.purpose: Reusable Cloudflare identity for validating zones and assisting with project DNS record changes.
resources.obtain: Cloudflare Dashboard → My Profile → API Tokens → Create Token. Start from the Edit zone DNS template, limit the token to the required zone(s), and create/copy the token once.
resources.validation: Bearer API token accepted by Cloudflare's token verification endpoint and authorized for the selected zone(s).
resources.security: Secret. Use a dedicated, zone-scoped token with only Zone:DNS:Edit and Zone:Zone:Read as needed; do not use the Global API Key or place the token in notes, source control, logs, or browser code.

resources.label: DNS records
resources.purpose: Routes public/custom domains and proves ownership.
resources.obtain: Cloudflare Dashboard → zone → DNS. When configuring Convex custom domains, copy the exact DNS record type/name/value returned by Convex.
resources.validation: Exact A/AAAA/CNAME/TXT record requested by the target provider.
resources.security: Use a zone-scoped API token and keep proxying off for verification records unless the provider explicitly supports proxying.

resources.label: Hostinger API token
resources.purpose: Reusable Hostinger API identity for validating account access and assisting with DNS changes in Hostinger-managed zones.
resources.obtain: Sign in to Hostinger hPanel → profile/account menu → API, then create an API token for this automation and copy it when Hostinger displays it. Keep the token associated with the minimum required account/domain access.
resources.validation: Bearer token accepted by the Hostinger API for a read-only check of the intended account or DNS zone before any change is attempted.
resources.security: Secret. Create a dedicated token, restrict its access to only the domains and operations required, rotate/revoke it when no longer needed, and never place it in project notes, source control, logs, or client-side code.

resources.label: DNS records
resources.purpose: Routes public/custom domains and proves ownership in Hostinger-managed zones.
resources.obtain: Hostinger hPanel → Domains → DNS / DNS Zone. Copy exact record values from the target service.
resources.validation: Exact A/CNAME/TXT record requested by the target provider.
resources.security: Change only the intended record set; preserve unrelated DNS records.

resources.label: GCP project ID
resources.purpose: Google Cloud namespace used for OAuth/API configuration.
resources.obtain: Google Cloud Console → project selector or IAM & Admin → Settings and copy Project ID (not Project name).
resources.validation: Google Cloud project ID, normally 6–30 lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens.
resources.security: Use a dedicated production project when practical and least-privilege IAM.

resources.label: OAuth client ID
resources.purpose: Public identifier for Google OAuth sign-in.
resources.obtain: Google Cloud Console → Google Auth Platform → Clients (or APIs & Services → Credentials) → select/create Web application client.
resources.validation: Google OAuth client ID, typically ending in .apps.googleusercontent.com.
resources.security: Client ID is not secret, but restrict its authorized origins and redirect URIs to real environments.

resources.label: OAuth client secret
resources.purpose: Confidential credential for Google OAuth server-side exchange.
resources.obtain: Google Cloud Console → Google Auth Platform → Clients → selected Web application client.
resources.validation: Google-generated client secret for the exact OAuth client ID.
resources.security: Do not paste this into Baton project notes/forms. Put it directly into the target deployment secret store (for Baton/Convex Auth this is AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET).

resources.label: Authorized redirect URI
resources.purpose: Allowlist for the server-side OAuth callback.
resources.obtain: Derive it from the deployed auth callback endpoint, then add the exact HTTPS URI to the Google OAuth Web client.
resources.validation: Exact HTTPS URI; no wildcard. For Convex Auth this is commonly https://<convex-site-host>/api/auth/callback/google.
resources.security: Register only known production/preview callbacks required by the app.

resources.label: Authorized JavaScript origin
resources.purpose: Allowlist for browser origins participating in Google OAuth.
resources.obtain: Use the public app origin (scheme + hostname + optional port, no path) and add it to the Google OAuth Web client.
resources.validation: Origin such as https://example.com, without a path or trailing callback route.
resources.security: Use exact production origins; remove obsolete localhost/preview origins when no longer needed.

resources.label: DOKU payment Client ID
resources.purpose: Merchant identifier used by DOKU Checkout/Direct API requests.
resources.obtain: DOKU Dashboard → Integrations → API Keys. Use Sandbox credentials for testing and Production credentials only after merchant activation.
resources.validation: DOKU Client ID issued for the intended merchant/environment.
resources.security: Sensitive merchant credential. Store it in the named DOKU Payment connection in MSO Integrations; Baton stores only binding/status metadata and the consumer deployment receives it only through a bounded secret-injection path.

resources.label: DOKU payment Secret Key
resources.purpose: HMAC signing secret for DOKU payment API requests.
resources.obtain: DOKU Dashboard → Integrations → API Keys, paired with the Client ID for the same Sandbox or Production merchant.
resources.validation: Secret Key paired with the selected DOKU Client ID; verify only through a bounded server-side provider check.
resources.security: High-value HMAC secret. Store only in MSO Integrations; never RR, Baton notes, Git, logs, frontend env, or MCP resources. Consumer deployments receive it only through a bounded server-side secret-injection path.

resources.label: DOKU payment environment
resources.purpose: Chooses DOKU Sandbox or Production API base without changing payment logic.
resources.obtain: Start with Sandbox; switch to Production only after production merchant credentials and payment notification settings are ready.
resources.validation: sandbox or production.
resources.security: Non-secret metadata. Never infer Production merely because credentials exist; make environment an explicit project decision.

resources.label: DOKU Payment Notification URL
resources.purpose: Receives authoritative server-to-server payment status notifications.
resources.obtain: Use the deployed HTTPS webhook route from the consumer project, then register that exact URL in DOKU payment settings for each enabled method as required.
resources.validation: Exact public HTTPS webhook URL that verifies DOKU signatures and handles idempotency.
resources.security: Non-secret endpoint, but the receiver must verify signatures before persisting or marking an order paid.

resources.label: DOKU MCP endpoint
resources.purpose: Streamable HTTP endpoint used by an AI/MCP client to call DOKU payment tools.
resources.obtain: Choose the official endpoint for the desired environment: Sandbox https://api-sandbox.doku.com/doku-mcp-server/mcp or Production https://mcp.doku.com/mcp.
resources.validation: Exactly one of the official HTTPS DOKU MCP endpoints.
resources.security: Endpoint is public metadata; credentials are separate and must stay in MSO/private client configuration.

resources.label: DOKU MCP Client ID
resources.purpose: DOKU merchant/brand identifier supplied to the MCP server.
resources.obtain: Use the DOKU Client ID assigned for MCP access in the DOKU environment you are connecting; the official MCP guide shows BRN-prefixed examples.
resources.validation: DOKU-issued MCP Client ID for the chosen environment.
resources.security: Treat as sensitive account metadata and keep it out of public RR/Baton content.

resources.label: DOKU MCP API Key
resources.purpose: Private API key authenticating DOKU MCP requests.
resources.obtain: Create/use the DOKU API Key assigned for MCP access in the selected DOKU environment.
resources.validation: DOKU MCP API key accepted together with the selected Client ID and endpoint.
resources.security: Secret. Never base64/embed it into committed MCP JSON. Keep it in MSO Integrations or another owner-only secret store and inject at runtime.
